gate.interpretation_floor: A7: exposure arm contrasts < 20 pp are never interpreted as substantive

metrics.A1: instrument-vs-human Cohen κ, census (overall); PASS κ≥0.60 and cluster-bootstrap LB≥0.40
metrics.A11: paraphrase intent: no unresolved contested text; CONDITIONAL ≤2 contested resolved; FAIL ≥3
metrics.A2: instrument-vs-human raw agreement, census; PASS ≥0.85 and LB≥0.70
metrics.A3: panel sensitivity on the 70 designed-detectable positives; PASS ≥0.90 and Wilson LB≥0.80
metrics.A4: panel specificity on all 100 negatives; PASS ≥0.85 and Wilson LB≥0.70
metrics.A5: inter-coder κ on the census semantic judgement (V6); PASS ≥0.50 and LB≥0.30
metrics.A6: max pairwise arm-differential instrument error; PASS ≤15 pp and largest-pair bound ≤25 pp
metrics.A9: label opportunity_class: inter-coder κ ≥0.80 (LB≥0.60) AND consensus-vs-label agreement ≥0.90

operationalisation_notes: A3 is computed on the 70 complete/partial planted positives. The 30 same-class replacement probes are a pre-declared blind-spot set reported separately (expected instrument sensitivity ~0); including them would make A3 structurally unpassable and would not test construct coverage.
A5 uses the census semantic judgement (present_0_1) that both coders make on every run; per-family κ is reported from the panel (40 cases per family).
A6 uses the 95 % cluster-bootstrap upper bound of the largest pairwise arm difference; the literal "CI excludes 0" diagnostic is also reported.
A9 requires consensus-vs-label agreement in addition to inter-coder κ, because two coders can agree with each other and both disagree with the frozen label.
